themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes Surge
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints spiked to 4 this week versus a 0.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 967% increase (z-score: 7.49)—suggesting either a new dumping problem or enforcement crackdown in Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights this week.
evidence: 4 abandoned bike complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (967% spike)
Z-score of 7.49 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Streetsblog NYC recently reported placard abuse in Downtown Brooklyn bike lanes (2026-04-13), suggesting bike infrastructure is a current neighborhood concern
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD or Sanitation about whether this reflects a real increase in abandoned bikes or stepped-up enforcement
Canvass bike racks in Fort Greene Park and Brooklyn Heights Promenade to document the scope visually

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Complaints Double
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints reached 32 this week compared to a 14.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 126% spike (z-score: 6.7)—pointing to emerging friction over Uber/Lyft operations or driver behavior in the district this week.
evidence: 32 for-hire vehicle complaints THIS WEEK vs. 14.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (126% increase)
Z-score of 6.7 indicates high statistical significance
Illegal parking (6,469 complaints over 90 days) remains the top 311 complaint type, and for-hire vehicles may be a subset driver
reporting_angles: Obtain TLC data on vehicle registrations and violations in CD 302 to see if there has been an influx of for-hire vehicles
Interview residents and business owners on Fulton Street and Atlantic Avenue about congestion and unsafe driving behavior

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Enforcement Spike
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints jumped to 6 this week from a 0.6 weekly average over 8 weeks—an 860% increase (z-score: 6.27)—suggesting new enforcement action or resident complaints about dining sheds in Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights this week.
evidence: 6 outdoor dining complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (860% spike)
Z-score of 6.27 indicates high statistical anomaly
Timing suggests possible new city enforcement push or resident activism around dining sheds post-pandemic
reporting_angles: Check with Sanitation or SLA to see if enforcement actions or permit reviews were initiated this week
Survey Myrtle Avenue and DeKalb Avenue dining sheds to document condition and occupancy rates

themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints reached 7 this week versus 1.1 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 522% surge (z-score: 4.63)—indicating possible tree removal or pruning violations in the district this week.
evidence: 7 illegal tree damage complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (522% increase)
Aligns with active construction: 1,180 DOB permits filed in past 90 days, which may be driving tree removal near development sites
reporting_angles: Obtain DOB violations data to correlate illegal tree damage complaints with active construction sites
Interview Parks Department about tree protection enforcement during the busy construction season

themes_detail.label: Police Discipline Complaints Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Investigations and Discipline (IAD) complaints spiked to 6 last week from a 0.2 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 2300% increase (z-score: 13.28)—suggesting a specific police conduct incident or escalation in civilian complaints against NYPD in the district last week.
evidence: 6 IAD complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2300% spike)
Z-score of 13.28 indicates extremely high statistical anomaly
Accompanied by 15 Real Time Enforcement complaints last week vs. 0.9 baseline (1614% spike, z-score: 13.41), suggesting possible enforcement operation or confrontation
reporting_angles: File FOIL requests for CCRB complaints and NYPD incident reports from the past 10 days
Interview community advocates and elected officials to learn if a specific incident triggered complaints
